original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Answer #3669 OQ2 for present-head flag 0: on the published #2089 promote/add/restore at events 5758/5759/5807, exhibit the self-owned host schedule S0 (owner=X0 on the full chart) for the X0 read, prove it is the unique owner among registers named by that ADD, prove the window touches no dirty helper (channel dirt restorations preserved), prove both endpoints remain at their unrestored channel finals (zero repayment toward initials), and prove that restoring X0 to its initial frame before the ADD breaks the published common-chart annotation.
scope_change_reason: #3669 OQ2 asks whether the published promote/add/restore admits an owner/host schedule for the X0 read that restores arbitrary dirt without repaying unrestored channel endpoints. Prior jwr404 readings show the frames, coefficient and that no owner field is named; #3349 shows endpoints unrestored. This package assigns the schedule and certifies dirt preservation, zero endpoint repayment and the pre-read restoration obstruction. Distinct from deferred flag0-head-span-schedule (+2 co-host at 3369) and from open #3532 flag-1 repair.
bottleneck_link: A legal I-G/2 completion needs an owner/host for every source read with dirty restoration. For flag 0's published tail cut, self-ownership on the unrestored full frame closes that local obligation without endpoint repayment; global hosting across all 4992 reads remains open.
stop_rule: Stop after S0 is certified with uniqueness, dirt non-touch, zero endpoint repayment and the pre-read obstruction, dual-scanned. Do not build a global 104-by-104 owner map, reprint #3669 chronology, retarget #3532 repair templates, or price a new kappa.
evidence: Event 5759 is add Y34 X0 -1/2 on FULL after promote 5758 and before restore 5807. S0 assigns owner=X0 (self) on host chart FULL. Among registers named by that ADD the unique source owner is X0. Window 5758..5807 has 48 Y34 adds and 2 Y34 transports, zero D/G/Q/C touches. X0 has no destination event after channel prefix (last write 1486). After 5807, X0 remains FULL and Y34 returns to RANK8 — both equal channel finals, neither equals its initial, so endpoint repay mass toward initials is zero. Forcing X0 onto initial [232] before 5759 conflicts with the ADD's FULL annotation. Coefficient matches CORRECTION-ROWS row 34 source 0. Selected kappa unchanged.

open_questions.question: Does the same self-owned zero-repay schedule extend uniformly to all 104 targets' promote/add/restore windows, or do some source reads require a copied host?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Flag 0 is one of 4992 source reads. A uniform self-owned pattern would discharge the global owner gap left by #2089; a counterexample would force host mass on some rows.
open_questions.first_step: Scan every target window in the augmented witness for dirty-helper touches and source destination events after the channel prefix.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package certifies only the flag-0 window.

open_questions.question: What is the minimum added host rank mass for a copied-host alternative that leaves X0/Y34 at channel finals but routes the 5759 operand through a fresh dirty helper?
open_questions.why_it_matters: S0 pays zero new host mass. A copied-host floor would price the gap between self-ownership and helper hosting under unrestored endpoints.
open_questions.first_step: Search nested helper paths from empty to FULL that acquire X0 before 5759 and restore dirt after, with X0 unwritten.
open_questions.blocked_by: No copied-host word is constructed here.
